overview: Modern Israel was proclaimed on 14 May 1948. This atlas starts its label in 1938, during British Mandatory Palestine, and repeatedly includes Gaza and the whole West Bank. That outline is not a map of recognized Israeli sovereignty, pre-1967 borders or present control. The last geometry ends in 2020; the state continues. This card distinguishes Israeli institutions and communities from Palestinians living under occupation, while following their connected histories through sources available on 23 September 2026.

periods.title: Before the state: an atlas mislabel
periods.summary: The imported name begins under the British Mandate; the modern state did not yet exist.

periods.title: Founding, war and new arrivals
periods.summary: State-building accompanied war, Palestinian displacement and Jewish immigration.

periods.title: Occupation and diplomacy
periods.summary: Israel occupied Palestinian territory in 1967; a treaty with Egypt followed in 1979.

periods.title: Agreements without a final settlement
periods.summary: Oslo created partial Palestinian self-government; Israel and Jordan made peace in 1994.

periods.title: War and its continuing aftermath
periods.summary: The October 2023 attacks and war in Gaza profoundly affected civilians; a ceasefire did not end humanitarian suffering.

sections.title: A state, its neighbours and a misleading outline

items.text: In 1947 the United Nations proposed partition into Jewish and Arab states, with a special international arrangement for Jerusalem. Israel’s establishment in 1948 came amid war. Many Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled from their homes. Independence for Israelis and dispossession for Palestinians are connected parts of this history; the atlas’s single colour cannot express them.

For Jewish survivors of the Holocaust, reaching a new home often followed years of waiting in displaced-persons camps. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum records that around 140,000 survivors entered Israel in the years after its founding. These were people rebuilding lives and families after persecution, not simply numbers added to a national population.

Israel occupied Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, in the 1967 war. In its advisory opinion of 19 July 2024, the International Court of Justice treated these as occupied Palestinian territory and found Israel’s continued presence unlawful. The imported polygon should therefore never be read as proof that these territories belong to Israel.

Israel removed its settlements and permanent military presence from Gaza in 2005. The ICJ explained in 2024 that this had not entirely ended its occupation-related obligations: those remained linked to its effective control. Troop locations alone do not settle the legal question.

Jerusalem needs its own qualification. Israel’s 1980 Basic Law designates it the capital and the seat of the Knesset, government and Supreme Court. The ICJ’s 2024 opinion treats East Jerusalem as occupied territory and rejects acquisition of territory through annexation. The location of government offices and international recognition of territorial claims are different questions.

The Knesset has 120 members, elected through national proportional elections. Seats are shared among party lists rather than assigned to 120 separate local constituencies. Basic Laws set out central institutions and rights. Looking at an election result therefore means asking how several parties might work together, as well as which party won the most seats.

A governing coalition is an agreement among parties willing to support a government. Partners negotiate policies and ministerial responsibilities; other parties form the opposition. Coalition bargaining helps explain why a small party can matter greatly when a government needs its votes. This describes how the system works, not whether any particular bargain is fair.

Diplomacy changed relationships that had once been defined by war. Egypt and Israel signed their peace treaty on 26 March 1979 after the 1978 Camp David negotiations. The negotiations also attempted a framework for Palestinian self-government, but that question was not resolved by the Egyptian-Israeli treaty.

The Oslo process brought mutual recognition between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization in 1993 and arrangements for limited Palestinian self-government. Further agreements divided responsibilities in the West Bank; they did not create a final peace settlement. Israel’s separate treaty with Jordan in October 1994 ended the state of war between those neighbours.

Mimouna, celebrated by many Moroccan and other North African Jewish families after Passover, brings friends and neighbours through open doors for sweet food. The National Library describes mufleta pancakes, singing and the next day’s picnics. Its undated photograph includes adults and children clapping and playing a tambourine. One useful party skill: leave enough room for both music and pancakes.

The National Library’s Mimouna account also describes migration from Morocco and settlement in development towns and villages. Families brought practices with them and adapted them in new settings. A festival can preserve memories of another country while becoming part of neighbourhood life in Israel; it does not mean every Israeli family has the same background or customs.

Ten families started a bilingual preschool in Haifa in 2012. According to the Hand in Hand school network, parents later petitioned the municipality to keep their children learning together. The programme moved through Arab and Jewish host schools and reached 271 pupils in the 2021/22 school year. Shared education here grew through persistent family organizing, including the very ordinary challenge of finding enough classrooms.

At Hand in Hand’s Jaffa school, an annual book week celebrates Hebrew and Arabic literature, with parents taking part in activities. Children can encounter the same neighbourhood through more than one language. This is a particular school community’s practice, not a claim that every school in Israel teaches in both languages.

A short Hebrew writing sample comes from the declaration of 14 May 1948: מדינת ישראל, transliterated Medinat Yisra’el, means “State of Israel.” These words appear in the Knesset’s official transcription of the founding document. This is a modern Hebrew witness with a known date, not an ancient inscription or a sample representing every language spoken by the country’s communities.

sections.title: Care, discovery and the journey after a flush

items.text: The European Observatory’s 2024 health-system account describes four nationwide health plans operating under National Health Insurance. They cannot reject enrollees, and resident coverage does not depend on whether contributions have been paid. Families obtain care through an organized system of plans and providers, rather than having to build a separate arrangement from scratch whenever a child gets sick.

Coverage still has important limits. The same 2024 study says foreign workers need private insurance, while adult refugees, asylum-seekers and undocumented migrants are outside National Health Insurance. Their children’s coverage depends on a parental contribution. A description of Israeli resident healthcare should not be stretched across everyone inside this atlas’s especially misleading outline.

Tipat Halav family health centres offer free preventive services for children from birth to six. Nurses check growth and development, help parents with questions and provide vaccinations and screening. A baby’s appointment can therefore include measuring, listening and conversation as well as a needle. The service is meant to help families notice needs early, before a problem becomes an emergency.

The water leaving a toilet has another journey ahead. The Central Bureau of Statistics describes Shafdan, the Dan Region wastewater project, as collecting and treating sewage, recharging treated water into groundwater and recovering it for reuse. Its agricultural tables record irrigation with treated effluent. Cleaning and reusing water requires infrastructure; this is not permission to put untreated sewage on crops.

Ada Yonath of the Weizmann Institute shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Venkatraman Ramakrishnan and Thomas Steitz for explaining ribosome structure and function. Ribosomes are the cell’s protein-making machinery. The researchers used X-ray crystallography to reveal their shapes in great detail. Their work also helped explain how some antibiotics interfere with bacterial ribosomes: a tiny machine can matter enormously to medicine.

sections.title: Conflict and civilian lives, with dated evidence

items.text: On 7 October 2023, Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups attacked Israel, killing civilians and taking hostages. A UN Commission of Inquiry reported in June 2024 that these actions included war crimes. Its separate investigation of Israeli operations in Gaza through December 2023 also found war crimes, including attacks on civilians and starvation as a method of warfare. These were the commission’s investigative findings, not criminal convictions of every person involved.

On 16 September 2025, the same independent UN commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Its analysis covered conduct from October 2023 through July 2025 and examined killings, destruction of living conditions and evidence of intent. This serious conclusion belongs to a UN fact-finding body; it should not be mislabeled a final judgment by the International Court of Justice.

A ceasefire announcement does not instantly rebuild homes or hospitals. OCHA’s report dated 18 September 2026, published on 21 September, described continuing danger in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Damaged housing, restrictions on essential supplies and shortages affecting health services continued to harm civilians. This dated account is evidence about occupied Palestinian territory, not a description of normal conditions for every household in Israel.

The same September 2026 report describes risks to water wells, wastewater workers and rubbish collection in Gaza, including temporary dumping sites that had run out of space. Sanitation depends on safe workers, fuel, equipment and access as well as pipes and toilets. Losing these services makes everyday tasks dangerous for families and adds public-health risks to the direct harm of fighting.

ending.text: Israel continues as a state; the atlas’s 2020 geometry cutoff is not a national ending. Evidence checked through 23 September 2026 describes continuing occupation and severe civilian suffering. Israeli and Palestinian communities retain distinct identities and histories despite this misleading outline.
